toroline.heading: ⚡ Toroline Hybrids
toroline.intro: Toroline's OMAKASE blends — poly/poly hybrids designed to be strung together. All sets come as two half-sets. String mains 1–1.5 kg lower than crosses for optimal balance.

gripAbout.kimony: About Kimony: Japanese grip manufacturer producing all grips in Japan (except the Tourna KGT141, made in USA). Renowned for their Hi-Soft polyurethane formula – widely considered the tackiest overgrip material available. The lineup spans wet/tacky overgrips (smooth, perforated, spiral-cushioned, textured), dry-feel overgrips for heavy sweaters, and premium replacement grips in both leather and synthetic. Hi-Soft EX is the flagship wet grip; Last Dry is the flagship dry grip.
gripAbout.yonex: About Yonex: The world's largest racquet sports manufacturer, producing grips in Indonesia with materials from Japan. The Super Grap line (launched 1987) is one of the best-selling overgrips globally – enough tape sold to wrap around the world six times. The lineup spans wet/tacky overgrips (smooth, cushion-ridged, antibacterial), dry-feel overgrips, and replacement grips in both leather and synthetic. Wet Super Grap (AC102) is the flagship overgrip; Ultimum Leather is the premium replacement grip.
gripAbout.tourna: About Tourna: Tourna built its reputation on the original blue dry overgrip — the most copied grip in tennis. Tourna Grip Original (XL-1) is the reference for sweat absorption (though with intentionally low durability — typical pro changes it every match). Tac and Mega Tac are the wet/tacky alternatives. Pro Tour Leather is the leather replacement grip, slightly more textured than Fairway Leather. For comparison: Kimony Last Dry has subtle tackiness and 3× the durability of Tourna Original; Yonex Dry Grap is similar to Tourna but slightly less absorbent.

gutIntro: Natural gut is made from cow serosa fibers — the most elastic, comfortable, and powerful string material available. Two configurations are practical: ⬆ gut mains (max power & feel; the Federer setup) or ⬇ gut crosses (max spin & control; the Djokovic setup, with longer gut life since crosses move less).
